name: IRF540NPBF
title: 100 V, 33 A N-channel HEXFET power MOSFET in TO-220
summary: A single N-channel enhancement-mode power MOSFET of the HEXFET family, rated 100 V drain to source and 33 A continuous at a 25 °C case, in a through-hole TO-220 package whose tab is the drain. On-resistance is at most 44 mΩ with 10 V on the gate; the threshold lies between 2 V and 4 V. The junction may run to 175 °C, and the part carries avalanche and diode-recovery dv/dt ratings.

circuits.description: Resistive-load switching test. A 10 V pulse generator drives the gate through RG, and the drain is loaded by RD from the VDD supply. VGS is observed at the gate and VDS at the drain; the delay, rise and fall times are taken between the 10 % and 90 % points of the two waveforms.
notes: VG.1 and VDD.1 are the positive terminals.
The caption reads Fig 10b; it should read Fig 10a.

circuits.title: Fig. 12a: Unclamped inductive test circuit
circuits.description: Avalanche test. The device under test is pulsed through RG for a time tp. A driver MOSFET, gated by a 15 V pulse through its own resistor, joins the VDD supply to the inductor L; a diode runs from the source return up to the driver's source and L. VDS is taken at the drain, and IAS at the 0.01 Ω resistor in the source return. The drain voltage rises to V(BR)DSS after tp (Fig. 12b).

circuits.title: Fig. 13b: Gate charge test circuit
circuits.description: Gate charge test. A 3 mA pulse from a current source charges the gate, and VGS is taken at the gate; the waveform is Fig. 13a. The drain current comes from a regulator built round a second MOSFET of the same type, whose gate is set by a 50 kΩ potentiometer across a 12 V cell. Two sampling resistors in the returns measure IG and ID.

circuits.title: Fig. 14: Peak diode recovery dv/dt test circuit
circuits.description: Body-diode recovery test. The device under test has its gate tied to its source. A driver MOSFET of the same type, switched through RG, sits below it with an inductor from their common node to VDD; a current transformer in the test device's source carries ISD. RG sets the dv/dt and the duty factor D sets ISD. Probe 1 is the driver gate drive (VGS = 10 V, or 5 V for logic-level parts), probe 2 the diode current from the current transformer, probe 3 the test device's VDS and probe 4 the inductor current, whose ripple is at most 5 %.

operation.text: The gate threshold is 2.0 V to 4.0 V at 250 µA. On-resistance is guaranteed at VGS = 10 V, 44 mΩ max at 16 A. The gate is rated to ±20 V. Charging the gate to 10 V with 80 V and 16 A at the drain takes at most 71 nC, of which 14 nC is gate-source and 21 nC gate-drain (Miller) charge; in Fig. 6 the Miller plateau sits near 4.5 V.
Driven by a constant gate current, VGS rises to the plateau while QGS is delivered, holds flat across QGD, then climbs to its final value VG; the total is QG (Fig. 13a).

The 33 A and 130 W ratings hold with the case at 25 °C; dissipation derates at 0.87 W/°C, and at a 100 °C case the continuous current is 23 A (Fig. 9). Junction to case is 1.15 °C/W max, case to a flat greased heatsink 0.50 °C/W typ, and junction to ambient 62 °C/W max. On-resistance roughly doubles from 25 °C to about 120 °C and reaches about 2.9 times at 175 °C (Fig. 4).

Single-pulse avalanche energy is 185 mJ calculated, from TJ = 25 °C with 16 A in 1.5 mH; the typical energy that destroys the part is 700 mJ. Repetitive avalanche is rated at 16 A and 13 mJ. The allowed single-pulse energy falls with starting temperature and with current, to zero at 175 °C (Fig. 12c). In the test the drain voltage rises to V(BR)DSS after the gate pulse tp ends (Fig. 12b).

The integral diode carries 33 A continuous and 110 A pulsed, drops at most 1.2 V at 16 A, and recovers from 16 A at 100 A/µs in 115 ns typ (170 ns max) with 505 nC typ (760 nC max) of recovered charge. Its recovery dv/dt is rated at 7.0 V/ns for ISD ≤ 16 A, di/dt ≤ 340 A/µs.

The four switching times td(on), tr, td(off) and tf are measured between the 10 % and 90 % levels of the VGS and VDS waveforms (Fig. 10b). With VDD = 50 V, 16 A and RG = 5.1 Ω they are 11, 35, 39 and 35 ns typical.
The tab is fixed with a 6-32 or M3 screw at up to 10 lbf·in (1.1 N·m). Leads may be soldered at 300 °C for 10 s, 1.6 mm from the case. The TO-220 package is not recommended for surface mounting.
The top face carries the part number, the Infineon logo, a line HYWWX (H for halogen free, YWW the date code, X the site code) and a four-digit assembly lot code.
